utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. And the last -- after the last meeting with the SDS in Prijedor, we had one more meeting in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So a few meetings in the month of May 1992, correct, or several? It's not important really.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a party meeting in early May in Kozarac, and the meeting that you're asking me about, after the ultimatum that was issued in Prijedor, was not a party meeting. It was a meeting of all local communes from that area, including the police, the Territorial Defence, representatives of the party, the local government office, and the citizens who wished to attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for purposes of the timeline again, May 22nd, 1992, there was an incident at Hambarine, approximately. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May 23rd, 1992, there was an announcement from the military regarding a military convoy passing through Banja Luka, through Kozarac, to Prijedor, an announcement that requested that the checkpoints which were established there by the various citizens of those communities be set back or removed 100 metres. Do you know anything approximately about that date, May 23rd, 1992, and this announcement that was made by the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an announcement immediately before the attack. I heard about it, but I'm not familiar with the text of the announcement. But I know that it was to that effect that you described, that the military would pass, that no obstructions should be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And May 24th, 1992, there was this incident in Kozarac that we're going to get back to, just trying to establish the timeline, correct, the attack, if you will, on the convoy, and then the attack on the town itself of Kozarac or the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the information which was provided by the military over the radio. Whether that was really the case, I don't know. All I know was that the army officially said that there had been attempts to prevent the military from passing, and that fire was opened on the soldiers. That was announced on the Serbian radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And on May 30th, 1992, sir, there was an attack on the town of Prijedor. Correct? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware of the attack, but I don't know the exact date. I assume it was on the 30th. You know this better than I do. At any rate, it occurred several days after Kozarac had been burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And one of the reasons is that in fact you, sir, from May 24th, 1992, up until the end of August or early September 1992 were actually on the run, in hiding, trying to save your own life as a result of the incident that occurred at Kozarac on or about May 24th, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, you're talking about an incident. Which incident? Excuse me, let me finish. It was not an incident. Everything was burnt down and torched. Thousands of people were detained, and you're talking about an "incident." Are you referring to the incident which was -- which involved the military who were stopped at the checkpoint, or the attack which involved a large number of forces, of troops? Maybe we do not understand each other. Maybe there has been misinterpretation or...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we do understand each other. I may have used an inappropriate word, and I didn't expect you to read into that word. Let me just try to restate the question, please. I'm not minimising what occurred by calling it an incident, I'm just trying to neutralise or use a neutral word so that we wouldn't exchange in a debate as to what had occurred. We'll have time for that. Approximately from May 24th, 1992 through end of August, early September, 1992, as you described, you were essentially a man on the run; you were going in to Trnopolje, you left Trnopolje, you went back into Trnopolje, then you were moved to Omarska, and then everything else that you described after that. Essentially, that's why you don't know what specifically had occurred vis-a-vis the attack on Prijedor on May 30th, 1992. Correct? Would that be a fair generalization?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards the attack which, as you said, occurred on the 30th of May, the attack on Prijedor, I know about this attack from what I heard over the Serb radio and the local commune radio, which functioned for a while. From Trnopolje, we could observe the fire. We could hear detonation, and we could see house in the village of Hambarine on fire. We could also see the smoke coming from the direction of the Prijedor town for several days after. All of the information that I have concerning this was what -- is what I was able to hear from the radio, from the reports of the Crisis Staff, or from what I was able to observe from my vantage point. As for my stay in that area, I said that I spent two months there, from approximately 24th of May up until the end of July, not September. At the end of July, I surrendered. I have explained the circumstances of that surrender, and was taken to the prison in Prijedor. Thereafter, I was taken to the prison in Omarska. I did not go to Omarska. I was taken to Omarska. There's a difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I agree with you, and I think my question said that you were taken to Omarska. But I agree. All I'm trying to do is establish dates. And the next date that comes to mined for me, at least, is this meeting that you had with Mr. Kupresanin in Banja Luka which was approximately, according to your testimony, sometime in September of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it occurred sometime in September. Whether it was in the first half of the month or in the second, I don't know. But I believe that it was in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, is it fair to state that from May 24th or thereabouts, 1992, until about September 1992, during that entire period, you simply did not know what position Dr. Milomir Stakic held, if any, and in fact you knew nothing about it and simply had no knowledge of that? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I knew for sure was that Mr. Stakic was a very important figure in the SDS. He had been appointed to a high-ranking position in the municipality as a prominent member of the SDS. I also knew that he held some function in the Serbian assembly, which was established sometime in January, I think. That is, in a parallel, ethnically pure, assembly of Prijedor. This is what I heard. I also heard his name being mentioned in the radio announcements which were broadcast at the beginning of the attack and during the days that followed. Of course, it is true that there were no longer any contacts with the SDS. It is also true that I could see certain things happening on the ground. I also talked to people who had heard things over the radio. But I did not have any direct insight as to the work of the government in Prijedor. However, I was familiar with the consequences of the orders issued by this government and the consequences of the work of this government and this authority on the ground. As for Mr. Stakic's function in, say, August or beginning of September, I didn't know that. When I saw him in Banja Luka, he was, for sure, occupying an important function. Otherwise, he could not have been there. This meeting was attended by high-ranking civilian politicians, military commanders, and I knew that he was an important figure in Prijedor. As I have already indicated, I had the opportunity to hear criticism by Mr. Srdic, who was not addressing me but other people, and who made mention of Mr. Stakic at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have an opportunity to discuss that at length hopefully. Sir, on May 28th, 2001, during your testimony in the Sikirica trial, page 3982, line 1, you were asked the following question: "Can you help me about this: There was an occasion when you saw together two politicians from Prijedor, a Mr. Srdic and a Mr. Stakic. Do you recall that?" Answer: "Yes, I recall that, true." Question: Line 5, "and can you tell us what, as far as you know, posts did those two men hold at the time when you heard this conversation," September of 1992, as you've described, answer by you, sir, at line 7: "I don't know that. No. I didn't know that. How the positions, how the posts were assigned in the Serb Democratic Party, or the structure of the Serb municipality established in the way that it was established, and knew nothing about it as of the 25th -- rather, the 24th May, 1992. I simply had no knowledge Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of that. But the fact itself that they turned up there when at the same time when Karadzic came to Banja Luka and when the foreign negotiator came there, that very fact speaks -- tells us that they did hold some posts, but what posts, what offices, I don't know." The period I'm interested in is from May 24th up until the time this meeting in Banja Luka that you were brought to, September 1992, you had absolutely no knowledge of what post Dr. Milomir Stakic held, not only for September and August, but you had no knowledge of what posts he held, if any, from May, end of May, June, July, August, and September. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I have already answered this question, and I have used the same -- I have answered in the same way as you have just read. I said that I had heard about these names, I knew that Mr. Stakic was an official with the Serbian assembly, and I know that he was with the Crisis Staff at the time of the takeover. What happened afterwards, whether there were any changes within these bodies, I don't know. I first heard about him as the president in Banja Luka on that occasion at that place, when Mr. Srdic said those words, when he accused him. And once again, I abide by what I said. These are facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back now, and thank you for that chronology. For my purposes, I'd like to end the chronology there, although there's other events obviously that transpired that are very important and indeed critical for both yourself and others. But for my purposes, I'm going to move on to different area. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you were shown a document that -- during your direct examination which was three pages, on the last page, it was Number 106, which was for the Territorial Defence of the area of Kozarac in which your name appeared. Correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes I do. I remember parts of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I got your testimony correctly, you were also shown that by the investigator during or prior to the time in which you signed your written statement, that three-page document. That was one of the things that the investigator shared with you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I saw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the investigator or whomever was there, did they show you the complete list or any additional lists of the people who were mobilised in the area of Kozarac in 1992, or is it your testimony that you were only shown this three-page document in connection with that particular issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. May I interrupt. We discussed Document S106, or what other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From my recollection, I believe it's 106, Your Honour. I don't have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Because I have 106 before me. It's only two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then it's not 106, Your Honour. It's a three-page document. We'll get to it. I'm just trying to put a context in. I apologise. It's a three-page document which we'll address in short order, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel. May we have, Your Honour, the usher show that document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, just indicate to me when you've had an opportunity to sufficiently review the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was shown this document in the Tadic case, as far as I can recall. But also in the Kovacevic case, and several days before this testimony, during the proofing. I think that there were more pages, but I didn't pay much attention to that because this document had already been produced in some other cases before the Tribunal. I didn't have any specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, how many more pages do you think there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't look at it for a long time. There were other papers there as well. I just recognise the document, and that was that. I think I said that the document had already been produced in other cases. There were some other documents stacked on the same pile.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, how many citizens from the area of Kozarac were actually members of the Territorial Defence in March or April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if it was more or less than a thousand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Territorial Defence before the war, or the extended Territorial Defence as it was in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The period that involves Exhibit S143, which your name appears on, what period was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that would be sometime in May, May 1992. This is a portion of the list of the expanded Territorial Defence. What the total of the names on the list was, including all of the villages and all of the relevant local communes, if that record is made or was made for the entire area of Kozarac, I don't know. The portion which concerns my village is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All I'm interested to know is do you know how many people were members of the Territorial Defence from the area of Kozarac, on or about the time period of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many people made themselves available to the Territorial Defence, nor what kind of weapons they had. But the fact is that people were called up if they wanted to join the Territorial Defence or not, and to state what kind of weapons they had, if any. So one should compile this type of list for every village, and it would be easy to calculate the total.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I've just done that actually, so thank you. Bear with me, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can have the Court instruct the usher to pass a document which was previously disclosed to the Defence under I believe 65 ter Number 629.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't believe we have it with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have extra copies, if the Court wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, can you just let me know when you've had an opportunity to review that document, and then I'll proceed with my questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can ask straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a list of persons who placed themselves at the disposal of the TO with weapons, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was this a list --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Signed personally. I am familiar with the part of the list that I signed. The other parts, I didn't have an opportunity to look through the other parts of this document. It's possible, though, that I've seen a page or two, but not -- I have not looked through the document in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if that's a complete list of the list of mobilisation, as it's identified as being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a list of persons who placed themselves at the disposal of the TO. How many of these persons were mobilised, I really couldn't say. I can't provide an accurate answer. I can only provide a partial answer. As far as my own local area is concerned, half of the persons from the Trnopolje Cesta list, which is also the section of the document that I myself signed did not receive the callup, nor was there time for the mobilisation to take place. And it was not possible to set up a unit with these men in the time given. I'm speaking about a large number of people from this list called "Trnopolje Locality Cesta".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's not complete. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think we've understood each other. Concerning my local commune or my part of the local commune, yes, the list is complete. But this is not a list of all mobilised persons. That's what I'm trying to say. This is a list of persons who said: "Okay, we'll defend. I place myself at the disposal of the TO. I have no weapon or I have a weapon." Then they added which sort of weapon exactly. And then they signed. These lists were to be used by the TO as a foundation, as some sort of basis for setting up TO units. There are people in this list who signed up and said they had weapons, but these people are aged 60 or 65. So these lists are not identical to TO units, but only contain persons who registered and expressed their willingness, if necessary, to join the TO and defend their own villages. This is not a list of the TO units. That's one thing I can say for sure. And also, I can ascertain, at least as far as my area is concerned, that these people were never organised as units. Perhaps they could have been, but there wasn't enough time and it just wasn't possible. I'm talking about the people on the Trnopolje Cesta list. Part of them were organised and functioned during the first day of attack but then broke down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Explain to me if you can or describe for me what the formal list of the territorial units looked like, what did that list look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, sir, as I've already said. I was not part of the structures commanding the TO or organising the TO. As any other citizen in the situation that occurred, I placed myself -- I declared myself available, and that's all I know. I also know, and you have asked me, I'll provide you with a specific example. Trnopolje Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you direct us to the page, please, that you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Trnopolje Cesta, page 2, page A5 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May we have the page again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A15, in the upper right corner. Here, for example, you have a gentleman called Duracak, Redzep. He's an elderly gentleman. He's not a man of military age. He's liable for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just -- and sir, I apologise for interrupting. All I want to do is ask you a couple of questions about the document, and then we'll discuss you at length, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd page of this document, A/1/2, there seems to be a stamp on the right-hand side of that document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Kozarac TO staff, TO Bosnia and Herzegovina, TO staff Kozarac. And then handwritten a list of 28 persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, if you could read the first line that starts with the word "stab" and then interpret that line slowly for us, and then the second sentence and then the third line, please, on that document you're looking at, A/1/2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "TO staff Kozarac." This is on most of the pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then the next line after that, TOBH, what is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a stamp. "Bosnia and Herzegovina TO,"" TO staff Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then "STOKozara" what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's S-T-O, that's "TO staff Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can direct your attention to page A/1/29, please, which I believe is the 29th page, if you just follow chronologically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I found the page. A/1/29.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the right side of that, there seems to be a word "Stanicki Vod." Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Stanicki. Sanitetski, it's medical. Sanitetski Vod, Medicinski Vod, which is medical platoon or medical unit. It's a unit providing medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is this list that we have here also one that included a military -- I'm sorry, a medical unit as reflected on A/1/29? A medical platoon, if you will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We've just established that. According to what is written here, and I can't see the TO staff Kozarac stamp here. So, on this page, there is no stamp. As far as I can see, it's all the same handwriting. Someone listed 13 people here and added "medical platoon." So this may have been added to this list from a different list where people were ordered according to numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And this, as far as you can see, sir, from the pages that are reflected there, up through and including page A/1/101 is for the Territorial Defence of the area of Kozarac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You said A/1/101.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Everything including up to the last page, which is A/1/101.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, according to the structure of the TO, it was organised on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. basis of parts of local communes, then the next level were local communes, and the headquarters were in the biggest local communes or in a town commune where there was a local office. In this case, in Kozarac. So all structures of the TO in this area, throughout the local communes in this area, had their files and their superior authority first in Kozarac and then in Prijedor. Accordingly, this is the TO staff Kozarac, but with competencies for the TO also in Kozarusa, Trnopolje, Jakupovici, and all other villages and local communes in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask that this exhibit be introduced into evidence as the next Defence exhibit. I apologise. I don't recall the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We provided it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This had, as I was informed a previous 65 ter number. It was only disclosed under this number. Then it is admitted into evidence as D11B. And please, on the list of exhibits may be marked that the pages A/1/5 to A/1/6 are identical, and following A/1/7 are identical with S143.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who -- and we can spend a few minutes now since we have approximately 10 or so minutes left, if you can tell me who Halil Seferovic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Halid Seferovic. I can't remember who he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, to the best of your recollection if Mr. Halid Seferovic was ever a member of the Territorial Defence in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that name. I can't remember the person by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the name of Sefer Halilovic, do you know anyone by that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that close after all. Maybe about 180 degrees at best. Yes, I had heard of Sefer Halilovic. I know he was the first commander of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When did he become the first commander of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately after the BH Army was first established. I can't remember the exact month when that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately what month and what year that occurred, sir? Was it in April of 1992, if I may be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April 1992, no. The BH Army, as far as I can remember, was not established in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then tell me when was it established.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think a couple of months later. We're talking about the BH Army. There was the BH TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when did that commence to exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The BH TO, I think 40 or 50 years ago when Tito won the war with his partisans, he established the republics of Yugoslavia. He established the army, the TO. So the TO had always been there, and it had commands at the level of all republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did the Patriotic League become formed, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Patriotic League, as a movement, I believe that the need to establish a patriotic movement was discussed in 1991. I can't remember the exact month, but I know that the BH Presidency provided an initiative for patriotic elements to join forces on the intellectual level. And with all their powers and capacities to advocate Bosnia and Herzegovina. I think formally there was an attempt to found the Patriotic League later on, but it was never really established as a full-fledged player. The situation just took a different turn. So the existing TO grew to such an extent that it could easily be transformed into a BH army. This was indeed done at a later date. I can't remember exactly when, but I suppose it was in the second half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After June of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After June of 1992, would that be your best estimate? Sometime after June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say really. About mid-1992, maybe it was even in the first half of 1992. I'm really not sure. But probably you should be able to find out about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just going back to Sefer Halilovic, was he the head of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I know, Mr. -- Just a minute. Let me recall his name. Karkin was the head of the TO. I think his name was Karkin. Whether there had been someone else in that position before, or after, I really don't know, but I know the TO was there. And I think Karkin was its head, but I'm not entirely concern about this. It's quite possible that at some point before the BH Army was established, Sefer had indeed taken part in the TO, but I never considered these issues very deeply, so I can't say anything much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have an opportunity to read a book or papers written by Mr. Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After he retired, he's a general who decided to enter politics, to go into politics. And as a politician, he had a party, and he published a book in which he provided his own interpretations of the war. I did not read this book, and I don't know about the theories in that book. I heard comments. Some people approved of the book, and some people criticised of it, but it very much depended on which of the sides involved was providing its opinion on the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, do you have any information or knowledge as to how many weapons or armaments Mr. Sefer Halilovic was in control of as the head of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina? In 1992, specifically April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've answered this, sir, and in quite some detail as far as concerns the TO. But I can't go into that because I simply don't know, especially not the level you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, if I may: Do you know if in March of 1992, the SDA party had established its own Crisis Staff? Do you know if it existed at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: March 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: March 1992. There wasn't a Crisis Staff. There were some ideas about one being set up, but these ideas never came to fruition, at least as far as I know. If there was anything happening at the local level, I really don't know. But in March 1992, we were functioning within legal institutions and officials were just simply doing their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this Crisis Staff, is it fair to say, then, that you heard of the term "Crisis Staff" not just through what you testified to, but also in connection with the SDA party? They were either thinking about forming it or actually had formed it in some of the local communes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, had a Crisis Staff of the SDA been founded in Prijedor, I would have been the second person to become a member of that Crisis Staff. There was no possibility of setting up such a Crisis Staff without me learning about it. The thing is very simple really.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just quickly on a couple of other issues if I can just try to squeeze them in, with respect to the armaments and weapons in Prijedor in 1992, do you know if there was a group of men from the SDA leadership who were actively soliciting funds, locally and abroad, in order to purchase arms and weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was there an organised group soliciting funds, and please, can you just specify which period you are referring to? Because this is very important. It's a very broad subject, much discussed. So please, if you can specify the period whenever you're asking a question, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In April and May of 1992, sir, did a group of men from the SDA party actively solicit funds, locally and abroad, for the purchase of -- for the purpose of purchasing arms and armaments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the existence of any such formal group by party orders. Please, if you would just --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- Let me finish. There was discussion about finding solutions to the situation. The area was blocked. There were no medicines. There was nothing available. A large number of people placed themselves at the disposal of the TO. There was a large number of Serbs who offered to sell weapons, Serbs from Omarska and from Prijedor. As I heard, even some Serbs from the barracks. There were proposals to borrow money so that people could buy weapons. It was only natural under the circumstances, which I'm sure you're quite familiar with. If there was any formal obligation concerning whatever persons to put together a fund for buying -- for purchasing weapons, I think the word "fund" is really ridiculous in this context because we had no institutions to use, nor was the money flow open at the time. We asked for assistance, or aid, not only from abroad, but we also appealled for political assistance in order to lift the blockade, both at the republic level as well as at the international level and wherever else we could. There is a human dimension to this entire situation. Take my example. I placed myself at the disposal of the TO. I had no weapon. I was terrified by the very idea that the military could just dash into my house in the middle of the night and kill my mother in front of me without me having a weapon to defend her. I wanted to defend my country, my mother, my sisters. It was the most natural need in a situation where we were just simply hermetically closed off and compelled to defend ourselves. People considered different models, different scenarios, but we never managed to organise what we had begun or to convince the SDS that they had no reason really to treat us the way they did. Today you spoke about an incident committed against the army on the 23rd in Kozarac, when the army fired their weapons, or -- excuse me -- on the 24th. There was no incident on the 23rd. But at least 300 soldiers had been inserted from the Ribnjak direction into Trnopolje and into the Serb villages surrounding in the process half of Trnopolje. But there was no incident really. So there was a process underway which, in essence, we could only observe, we could pray to God and pray to the Serbs to have mercy and not to kill people for no reason at all. And again, I must be sincere with you. We really hoped that all that was happening at the political level, at the federal level, and at the international level would help to turn the events around. There was the decision by the federal army eventually that they would withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina. We hoped that this would eventually come true, this news was encouraging for us. But no changes took place, and the JNA just continued to do what it had been doing up to that point. And in this sort of situation, you asked me about people putting together funds. If people had been able to give birth physically to weapons, they would have. We had blacksmiths, who shod horses, make weapons for the first time in their lives. We had all these people involved to try to look for barrels, to try to forge, literally make weapons, to get gun powder from the hunters and to improvise some sort of weaponry. We just sat by and waited. I must return to this now. I had, I think, a need and a moral obligation, if I'm abusing your patience, please forgive me. Can we just return to the previous question. There was a number of ideas, people said: "Come on, let's link up somehow. We must see what's happening. We must see what's in the making. We're not being treated any differently from how the other towns in Bosnia and Herzegovina were being treated. There's bound to be a massacre." People were searching for a solution, but they couldn't find one, and there was nothing to be done. We were just left to our own devices. Let me tell you another thing: If there was any serious form of organisation, of structure, or any considerable amount of weapons available, what kind of army would have been able to just wipe off the whole area within 24 hours? It was celebrated as a great historic achievement. We triumphed over tens of thousands of extremists in such a short time. Your Honour, please forgive me. I know that it's not desirable in Court. I did get slightly emotional. But also in the light of what we were speaking about, I just want today clarify a couple of my own answers. And after all, naturally, regardless of all that has happened, I do not want in the least for anyone to be convicted more than Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is their just share, not a single bit more, and I stand behind these words. They are a principle for me in my life. But please don't ask me to judge matters I'm not qualified to judge or events that I did not witness. Then please, ask me "what's your opinion, why did this happen" but ask no further than that. Please. Thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you made quite clear what you wanted to express. And unfortunately, we have to break for today, until Monday, 10.00. And may we please hear what is now to be expected on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to ask if Mr. Sejmenovic could be given an indication of how many longer cross-examination will be. Because he was expecting to leave today. He wasn't aware that the Court wasn't sitting on Friday, I don't think, because nobody has been able to speak to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was the information available one month ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know, Your Honour. But clearly we thought it would be finished. Otherwise, Your Honour, what is intended on Monday is that Mr. Sejmenovic will continue. The other witness will be testifying in the other case still. So at the moment, things are up in the air. The only problem will arise is if that witness cannot give his evidence in here on Tuesday and be finished on Tuesday. That's the problem that will arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's the understanding, we commence on Monday morning with the continuing cross-examination, and then I understand that the Defence is prepared to have a break in order to facilitate proceedings to allow the other witness to come in immediately, and then have this witness Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And from my perspective, I think it will be necessary to continue with the cross-examination Wednesday. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honour. We'll try our best, but I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know part of this is the difficulty of the other witness. But really I think, maybe we ought to ask Mr. Sejmenovic, I think it would be very unfair to keep Mr. Sejmenovic here until Wednesday. I really would hope that, as Your Honours indicated on a number of occasions to me, the Defence could get to the point and they could finish Mr. Sejmenovic on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But I think we have to balance. Four days and 90 minutes, and on the other hand, there were several points, several very important points, and I think the witness knows about his own importance for the case. And therefore, I would ask for your understanding that it may be necessary that you stay here until Wednesday. And I appreciate that you do so. And let's proceed this way, anticipating that it may be, emphasise, may be necessary, that we continue with the cross-examination on Wednesday. So let's call it a day now. And on Monday, 10.00, we resume. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 7.10 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
